(28BYJ-48 BiPolar, 28BYJ-48 UniPolar), 2x DISPLAY? (I2C_OLED SSD1306). The output reports total_components=5 (counting only 5 unique refs), which severely undercounts the actual component density. The BOM also shows only 5 entries with qty=1 each instead of reflecting true quantities.

assertions.description: INCORRECT: The I2C_OLED(SSD1306) component is classified as type='diode' in the BOM and component_types statistics. An OLED display module is not a diode. This misclassification is due to the lib_id 'kdn_kicad:I2C_OLED(SSD1306)' not matching any of the analyzer's IC/connector/display patterns. The component_types shows diode=1 instead of ic=1 (or a display subtype).
assertions.incorrect_review: rewrite (TH-105, 2026-11-06): diode=1 today is DISPLAY? I2C_OLED(SSD1306), the only diode; correct output has no diode
assertions.migration_note: TH-105: re-anchored to the value the review calls correct (was {"path": "statistics.component_types.diode", "value": 1, "op": "equals"})

The proliferation is caused by multiple unannotated duplicate U? instances all sharing the same reference, creating spurious net connections. Only 1 genuine I2C bus (DISPLAY? OLED on SCL/SDA) likely exists. The I2C entries on '+3.3V' and 'GND' as SCL/SDA nets are clearly erroneous.
